newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: European trade body urges advertising deregulation.
newsitem.headline: European trade body urges advertising deregulation.

text.p: Europe's biggest advertising trade body on Thursday urged an end to restrictions on the advertising industry that it said went against the trend to liberalise and deregulate other businesses in the region.

Albert Winninghoff, the president of the European Association of Advertising Agencies, told an industry conference the advertising sector had been unfairly singled out for tough restrictions in some countries.

He told the annual European conference of the International Advertising Association the restrictions contradicted the European Union's stated goal of ensuring the free flow of goods, services, people and capital among its member states.
"Somehow advertising seems to be excluded from the liberalisation and deregulation wave," Winninghoff said.
He said some European countries unfairly restricted advertising by banning or restricting "message content" and access to media for certain products.
Some rules designed to protect consumer privacy concerning buying habits and other personal details sometimes unfairly hampered the growing business of database marketing, he said.
"Instead of harmonizing liberties -- which lies at the core of the European Union -- advertising is singled out for harmonisation of restrictions," Winninghoff said.
He said France, for instance, wanted its current tough restrictions on alcohol and tobacco advertising to be adopted by other European countries.
Sweden wants to "export" its ban on advertising aimed at children, Winninghoff said.
"And the European Commission itself has a couple of nasty initiatives in the works as well," he told the opening of the two-day conference, without elaborating.
Many European countries have self-regulatory advertising industries, but some consumer groups have pressed their governments and the European Commission to implement statutory regulation.

Winninghoff urged the U.S.-based International Advertising Association and other regional and global advertising bodies to fight for the right to advertise products and services that are legally produced, distributed and consumed.
With consumer markets becoming increasingly competitive and increasingly global, advertisers and ad agencies say they want to be able to spread their commercial message freely across borders.
